He's playing to a wonderful 11-to-1 touchdown -to-interception ratio, while completing 76.7% of his passes. Do I think those numbers are sustainable? Probably not, but it's still worth mentioning. The one thing that I worry about him, though, is how often he's been sacked. Virginia's offensive line has been a sieve, ranking in the bottom 20 in sack percentage and letting opposing defenses get to its quarterbacks nine total times. And this is a team that primarily likes to run the ball. The Cavaliers are ranked 74th in pass attempts per game, while ranking eighth in rushing attempts. So, yes, there's concern there, because there's nothing spectacular about Virginia's run game. It likes to split the ball between a running back committee because Jekail Middlebrook hasn't separated himself from the pack. Middlebrook hasn't proven to be an effective distance runner, and Xay Davis and Xavier Brown clearly have the efficiency edge. On another note, I really like what the Cavs are doing defensively. They have a deadly secondary led by Jacobie Henderson and Brandyn Hillman. Hillman has already recorded three interceptions and a forced fumble. Not only that, Virginia is one of the best teams in standard down metrics, ranking second in explosiveness allowed and eighth in PPA. Its work against the pass is unsurprisingly its best attribute with Henderson and Hillman, and the Cavs rank fifth in PPA allowed and 10th in success rate allowed. Color me confused on these Seminoles. They're one of the most difficult teams to read in this Group of 6. They started off the season awfully slow against New Mexico State , despite winning, and then got into a slugfest against both SMU and Alabama. And at one point, it seemed like FSU was poised to beat Alabama for the second consecutive season, this time in Tuscaloosa. Quarterback Ashton Daniels seemed like he was lost in the pocket after the first two weeks, played a strong first half against Bama, then threw three interceptions against the Tide. The following week, he threw another pick against Central Arkansas, no less. This is a boom-or-bust team. There's a reason why the Noles have one of the most explosive offenses in the FBS, yet sit 11th in the ACC . Running back Ousmane Kromah has been a star, rushing for 6.4 yards per catch and five touchdowns. Receivers Duce Robinson and Jayvan Boggs are big-time playmakers, but because Daniels is so volatile, they can't be a big part of the offense. Defensively, this is a squad that has some active hands. Currently, 11 players have recorded a pass breakup, including two each from defensive backs Ja'Bril Rawls and Ma'Khi Jones. However, that's all the nice things you'll hear from me about their defense. Florida State ranks near the bottom in nearly every standard down metric. I'm inclined to take Virginia here. Simply, I'm riding with the better team. While this game is being played in Tallahassee, I don't think the Seminoles are good enough defensively to stop the Cavaliers. That's not to say Virginia is perfect, but because Florida State has such a hard time defensively, I see Virginia's offensive line using this game as a "get right" moment. The one concern I have with picking the Cavs is the Daniels factor. He's been known to take off and run. In Virginia's sole loss against West Virginia, the Cavs got chewed up badly by dual-threat quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., and I can definitely see Daniels using that to his advantage. If Virginia can learn from that loss and not make the same mistakes, this is a prime opportunity to lay the points with the Cavaliers. Pick: Virginia -2.5 Be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis!

Against non-Power4 opponents this season, Virginia allowed less than 100 yards rushing in threegames. However, against West Virginia, the Mountaineers shredded the Cavaliersdefense for 247 rushing yards and three touchdowns. So, Virginia is weakagainst the run at times. Some games that were previously near-locks (Duke and Wake Forest) are now likely to be high-stakes matchups in the ACC standings. However, the overall outlook remains about the same. ESPN predicts the Cavaliers to go 10-2 (8-1 ACC), which would be enough to earn a spot in the ACC title game as long as three of Miami, Clemson, Pitt and SMU lose at least one or two more ACC games. Here is the game-by-game outlook: At Florida State: 58.4% chance of victory (Previously 53.9%) The Seminoles remain one of the bigger unknowns in the conference. After a brutally frustrating home loss to SMU, Florida State came a few plays away from upsetting Alabama on the road. This week's game is a true tipping point for the Seminoles - and Virginia. Syracuse: 84.3% chance of victory (Prev. 77.3%) Quarterback Steve Angeli has struggled. A lot. His interception total nearly matches his touchdown total, and Syracuse's season might be over before it started. The Orange are in desparate need of a win, more so than just about any other team in the Power Four. At SMU: 45.6% chance of victory (Prev. 34.6%) The Mustangs have looked more like an eight-win team than a Playoff team so far. As a result, this game has gone from near-impossible to a true toss-up. Virginia has an increasingly decent chance to steal the upset in Dallas and take pole position in the ACC title race. Duke: 58.7% chance of victory (Prev. 73.6%) Duke has been one of the bigger positive surprises in the conference. Its offense has picked up where it left off (despite a massive portal exodus), and the defense has taken major strides. Right now, the Blue Devils could very well run the table and return to Charlotte. At Wake Forest: 58.3% chance of victory (Prev 62.5%) Aside from Duke, Wake Forest has been the biggest pleasant surprise in the ACC this year. The Demon Deacons nearly upset No. 4 Miami, and just upset No. 16 Louisville. This Halloween bout looks increasingly dangerous for the Cavaliers. Cal: 90.6% chance of victory (Prev. 90.8%) This number might still be too high. Yes, the Golden Bears have sputtered out of the gate, but there is too much talent on this offense for Cal to be mediocre. North Carolina: 74.1% chance of victory (Prev. 69.8%) Bill Belichick's Tar Heels team is elite defensively. Once again, all questions reside on the offensive side of the ball. Can North Carolina keep pace with Virginia? At Virginia Tech: 53.1% chance of victory (Prev. 49.4%) In a shocking development, the Cavaliers' odds continue to rise in this game. Virginia Tech as a home underdog is a great surprise - but Virginia does have a loaded roster with the ability to steal a win in Blacksburg, Va. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan Skip to main content Recruiting In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. home.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
home.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan Skip to main content Recruiting In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. The second half was a complete 180, as Kentucky shut out South Alabama and pulled away for a 45-21 victory, and the victory improved Kentucky to 3-1 overall and 1-1 in SEC play. Now, the Wildcats will take on a struggling South Carolina team on the road. The last time Kentucky was on the road, the Wildcats defeated then-No. 9 Texas A&M, 31-21, in College Station. The victory showed how strong Kentucky's defense can be while also giving quarterback Kenny Minchey an opportunity to show what he can become as he continues to develop under first-year head coach Will Stein. South Carolina Gamecocks (2-2, 0-2) The Shane Beamer era is facing increased pressure in Columbia, as South Carolina enters the matchup on a seven-game SEC losing streak. The Gamecocks' last SEC victory came against Kentucky on Sept. 27, 2025, when South Carolina defeated the Wildcats 35-13. South Carolina opened the 2026 season with a dominant 57-0 victory over Kent State, but the Gamecocks have since struggled against SEC competition. South Carolina lost 41-34 at home to Mississippi State before falling to Alabama 49-18 on the road this past weekend. The loss to Alabama dropped the Gamecocks to 0-2 in SEC play. Now, Kentucky comes to Columbia, making this a potentially significant game for Beamer and the Gamecocks. Kentucky is also looking to snap a four-game losing streak against South Carolina. Doing so under Stein would give the Wildcats another significant road victory during his first season. South Carolina will also be without star EDGE Dylan Stewart, who has been suspended indefinitely by Beamer and more than likely will not play against Kentucky. Stewart's suspension came after the Gamecocks' loss to Alabama, during which he threw a punch at Alabama tight end Josh Ford and had a heated interaction with South Carolina's coaching staff. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains one of South Carolina's biggest offensive weapons. The dual-threat quarterback opened the season with 270 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Gamecocks' win over Kent State. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is another player Kentucky will need to account for. Harbor returned to South Carolina for the 2026 season alongside Sellers and remains one of the team's most important receiving threats. Junior running back Matt Fuller is also a name to watch in the South Carolina backfield after showing his ability as both a runner and receiver. ESPN gives Kentucky a 42.1% chance of winning. My Early Prediction: Kentucky has already proven it can win on the road after defeating then-No. 9 Texas A&M. Why can't the Wildcats do it again? South Carolina is on a seven-game SEC losing streak and will be without Stewart, while Kentucky enters the matchup ranked No. 24 in the AP Top 25 and coming off a dominant second half against South Alabama. picks.headline: Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers?
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CFB Week 5 live updates Judge not on ALDS roster NFL Week 4 injury tracker WNBA semifinals preview MLB Division Series preview Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction: Can Wildcats solve LaNorris Sellers? Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will look to justify its No. 24 ranking at South Carolina on Saturday. The Wildcats are ranked for the first time in almost three years, but if they don't snap a four-game losing streak to the Gamecocks, the stint in The Associated Press Top 25 will not last long. Will Stein's squad has already proven capable of winning in a raucous road environment at Texas A&M, but Stein has been clear he does not believe UK's performance in a win over South Alabama last week was up to the program's standard. Can Kentucky build momentum in advance of a homecoming game against LSU? Can Stein flip the script in a series that has often gone a long way in determining the success of each team's season? Here is what you need to know ahead of the matchup . Kentucky cracked the AP Top 25 for the first time since October 2023 this week but remains in the "others receiving votes" portion of the Coaches Poll. That distinction offers a glimpse at the work the Wildcats still need to do to earn national respect. Upsetting Texas A&M put UK in the spotlight for a week, but now there are real questions about how good the Aggies are. Combine the sluggish opening to the win over South Alabama, and Kentucky's hold on a spot in the Top 25 appears tenuous. "It's cool and all, but I mean that thing shifts every single day," offensive guard Tegra Tshabola said. "We keep focusing on that, we won't be in there long." A win at South Carolina might not move the needle much in terms of national perception since the Gamecocks are 0-2 in SEC play, but it would at least ensure Kentucky remains ranked for its homecoming matchup against LSU next week. Despite UK's spot in the top 25, South Carolina is a three-point favorite as of Friday morning. "I think it's more important for the fans than anything," Stein said. "Our guys got to go play well. I'm not really sure why they rank people this early in the season. There's a lot of games left. It's about playing well on Saturdays. Not letting that dictate how we play. We should play to our standard regardless." Kentucky defensive lineman Kahlil Saunders (92) tries to wrap up South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) during a game at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Saturday, Sept. 27, 2025. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Another test for UK defense South Carolina was blown out 49-18 at Alabama last week but averaged 45 points per game in its first three games. That stretch included a 41-34 loss to Mississippi State. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers entered the season as a top-50 NFL draft prospect, according to The Athletic, but his performance has been mixed so far. Through four games, Sellers has completed 62.1% of his passes for 833 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed for 244 yards and one touchdown on 36 carries. Sellers' stats are boosted by his performance in the season-opening 57-0 win over Kent State in which he completed 19 of 23 passes for 270 yards and three touchdowns. In two SEC games, Sellers has thrown three touchdowns and three interceptions. He also completed just 10 of 23 passes for 96 yards in the Week 2 blowout of Towson but did rush for 119 yards in that game. "I think he's extremely dynamic," Stein said. "He can make every single throw. Big arm, and then when he pulls the ball down, he's very dangerous. They also have really good skill players on offense, so it'll be a big task for our defense to go against these guys, especially in their place." Sellers has given Kentucky fits the last two seasons, completing 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He rushed for 81 yards on 14 carries last season. Kentucky football injury report Stein downplayed any long-term concerns about UK players who picked up injuries in recent weeks, but the Wildcats will be without at least one key player in Columbia. Junior wide receiver DJ Miller, who was injured while trying to run a deep route against South Alabama, was initially listed as doubtful on the SEC availability report then downgraded to out on Friday. Long snapper Cole Marszalek, backup cornerback Grant Grayton, offensive guards Jay Clark and Aba Selm and linebacker Tavion Wallace were also listed as out Fifth-year linebacker Alex Afari was also listed as unavailable Friday after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dismissed the temporary injunction that had made him and dozens of other athletes eligible in their lawsuit against the NCAA for a fifth season of eligibility. The good news for UK is star defensive tackle Tavion Gadson, who missed the South Alabama game, was not included on the availability report, signalling he is expected to play at South Carolina. Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction A fast start could be particularly important Saturday with frustrations high among South Carolina fans. If Kentucky can take control of the game early, the atmosphere could grow tense for Shane Beamer and Gamecocks players. A high-scoring affair seems likely, but Kentucky's experience at Texas A&M should help prepare the Wildcats for the moment. Kentucky 35, South Carolina 28. The last word "I don't know a stadium in this league that's not going to be loud. … I would imagine every stadium we go into is going to have crazy fans that are really passionate and make third downs and fourth downs really difficult on the opposing offense. So, it goes back to how do you play good football? Learn how to not beat yourself before you go in. Have to be elite in communication, in operation, in and out of huddles. No huddles, cadence, all that stuff is going to be critical for our success. The Wildcats (4-1, 2-1) forced a punt and got the ball back with 2:08 to play but didn't score, allowing the game to go into overtime. Both teams scored on their first try but Kentucky went for two on theirs, winning the game. Sellers finished 20-of-36 for 226 passing yards, one touchdown and 147 rushing yards. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus CFB Week 5 live updates Judge not on ALDS roster NFL Week 4 injury tracker WNBA semifinals preview MLB Division Series preview Three Bold Predictions for When the South Carolina Gamecocks Take on Kentucky Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) calls for the snap during the first quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alex Joyce Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:17 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). A good run game can open passing windows for an offense that has struggled in that department for the last two weeks. I expect this to be the case and for Gamecocks to see a better attack than they have in recent weeks. Sep 19, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks wide receiver Mazeo Bennett Jr. (3) attempts to get around Mississippi State Bulldogs safety Isaac Smith (2) in the second quarter at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LaNorris Sellers finishes with no interceptions In the last three games, Sellers has four interceptions , two of which came against Mississippi State. On the other side, Kentucky has been great this season at creating turnovers. On paper this is a matchup that favors the Wildcats. However I believe Seller ends his interception streak this week and keeps this passing game on track. Gamecocks rush for 200+ In their two SEC games this season, Kentucky gave up 155 yards and three touchdowns to Bama. Against Texas A&M they gave up 187 yards and two touchdowns. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. The Wildcats are 3-1 and have a big-time road upset as they took down the Texas A&M Aggies, who were ranked #9 at the time. While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. The Gamecocks are 2-2 so far this season, with losses to Alabama and Mississippi State. Fans in Columbia are starting to get really frustrated with the way this team is playing, and some feel that the end could be near for Shane Beamer. Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; South Carolina Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer reacts to a play during the first quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the Wildcats are able to win this game, it could be bad for Beamer, and the administration at South Carolina could have a big decision to make. It's clear that Kentucky winning this game would be huge for the Wildcats chances of winning a Bowl Game. ESPN's Matchup Predictor does not like the Wildcats chances of going on the road and taking down the Gamecocks. ESPN only gives the Wildcats a 42.1% chance to go on the road and take down the Gamecocks. South Carolina has taken some ugly losses early in the season, but they still have a lot of talent on this roster. The Gamecocks have a very good quarterback in LaNorris Sellers, who has given Kentucky issues during his time in Columbia. If the Wildcats aren't able to bottle up Sellers, he could give the Cats problems once again. Sellers is a quarterback who can use his legs and arm to beat a team. Kentucky needs to keep containment and make sure he stays in the pocket. If he gets outside of the pocket, this is where he can hurt teams. Sep 26, 2026; Lexington, Kentucky, USA; Kentucky Wildcats head coach Will Stein looks on during the third quarter against the South Alabama Jaguars at Kroger Field. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This feels like a game that Mark Stoops would struggle in, so BBN is hoping that with Stein in charge, things are going to go a lot better in Columbia for the Wildcats. If they do win, a massive game will be set up between the Wildcats and LSU Tigers, with the Power K making a return. This is a big weekend for both Stein and Beamer, but Kentucky fans are hoping the Wildcats will be heading back home with a big-time win. If Kentucky wins, Stein has a great shot at making a year-one bowl. away.headline: Initial Injury Report for Kentucky at South Carolina
away.blurb: A big name on the injury report is wide receiver DJ Miller, who is dealing with a soft tissue injury that caused him to just play eight snaps against South Alabama. He is listed as doubtful. Miller had a breakout game against Texas A&M and has been the second best wideout behind true freshman Kenny Darby. He has dealt with soft tissue injuries throughout his young career at Kentucky, he was sidelined last season as a true freshman because of it and dealt with something similar this offseason as well. This is certainly something to monitor. Other than Miller, Jordan Castell is the other starter listed, but he is probable, so not a big worry. Ty Bryant, the other starting safety, isn't listed on the report despite dealing with a shoulder injury over the past few weeks. Outside of Dylan Stewart serving a suspension, South Carolina is pretty healthy across the board. There aren't many notable names on this list for the Gamecocks. Defensive lineman Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy is questionable, and the other potential key player out of action. Kentucky could be slightly undermanned in this road test that is a massive game for both teams. These injury reports will continue to be updated throughout the week, but the initial injury report suggests Kentucky could potentially be down a couple key starters on Saturday. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:22 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One of the biggest ACC games of the season takes place Saturday night as No. 4 Miami heads to Death Valley to take on Clemson . Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. (Patrick Breen/The Republic) 1 / 29 Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney Tait Reynolds, Clemson football freshman quarterback for Dabo Swinney How much of this game will have to be decided by Reynolds, who is a freshman? This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Clemson vs. Miami scouting report Where Clemson has an advantage: Miami hasn't faced a secondary as good as Clemson's. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. Miami generated pressure on 60.8% of Wake Forest's dropbacks in its last ACC game, and Reynolds is 20 of 46 for 175 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions when he's under pressure or blitzed. away.headline: Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson?
away.blurb: The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . The final injury report revealed which Hurricanes will be back tonight. Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out according to Saturday's final injury report: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Xavier Lucas, DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas moved from questionable to out on Friday night. After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight, but his status changed from questionable to out Friday night. away.headline: Miami football injury struggles open new opportunities
away.blurb: Week three’s road trip to Wake Forest decimated Miami’s health, losing backup running back Marty Brown (knee) and WR3 Joshua Moore (upper-body) for the season. Crucial starters in Ahmad Moten Sr., WR Malachi Toney, and RB Mark Fletcher all got banged up to a more limited extent. The position group most heavily impacted by injuries is the secondary with Frederique, Lucas, Ja’Boree Antoine out for extended periods with Damari Brown nicked up as well. While sophomore safety Bryce Fitzgerald theoretically plugs in well at corner due to his length and athleticism, it has been glaringly obvious that he is playing out of position so far this season. Fitzgerald referred to him as a “freak of nature” after his first four games, indicating that his expanded role is not likely to diminish even when the guys in front of him return. Sophomore wideout Malachi Toney is on pace for 102 catches, 1,700+ yards, and 18 touchdowns following his record-breaking freshman season. However, despite this elite production from the Heisman candidates, the offense has lost multiple weapons with Brown and Moore out for the season. The Hurricanes are lucky to have the two best statistical receivers in the country from a year ago in the same room, and need to maximize their talent. Expect Dalyn Upshaw and freshman Somourian Wingo to round out the Canes receiving rotation in Moore’s absence. © 2025 The Miami Hurricane is an independent, student-run organization that operates out of Coral Gables, Florida. Miami immediately lost two starting defensive backs in its season opener with OJ Frederique (shoulder) and Xavier Lucas (undisclosed) for multiple weeks. away.headline: Why the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes Should Limit Starters Returning From Injury
away.blurb: MIAMI, Fla. – After missing last Saturday's 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium, the No. 4 Miami Hurricanes are set for the return of running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. (both seniors) against Clemson , but it should be taken with caution. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He was the primary backup to Fletcher Jr., but an opportunity for more snaps presents itself. For starters, Fletcher Jr. shouldn't return to a heavy workload. As the Hurricanes' go-to running back, the 21-year-old's long-term availability is valuable. Fletcher Jr. proved to turn things up a notch when the lights got brighter in last year's historic run to the National Championship game. Plus, Pringle Jr., Mallory, and Wheatley-Humphrey can gain experience playing college football in a hostile environment. Memorial Stadium, otherwise known as Death Valley, is one of the sport's most historic venues. Pringle Jr. only logged six snaps in last year's College Football Playoffs and Wheatley-Humphrey had 19, but only on special teams. As Hurricanes offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson looks to spread the workload in the backfield, this Saturday presents an opportunity to play at least four different running backs. They will be facing Clemson 's junior linebacker, Sammy Brown , who was the ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. Moten Sr. is off to a slow start this season. Thus far, in 91 snaps across three games, he's logged three total tackles, a solo and two assists, 0.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks, and four pressures. Moten Sr. suffered a left shoulder injury against Wake Forest, left early, then returned to play the rest of the game. Despite having first-round projections in the 2027 NFL Draft, the Hurricanes still need the star defender healthy in the long run. It presents an opportunity for sophomore Jarquez Carter and junior Keona Davis, who have been serviceable in reserve roles, to step up. The Hurricanes have great depth at both running back and defensive tackle. home.blurb: The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . The final injury report revealed which Hurricanes will be back tonight. Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out according to Saturday's final injury report: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Xavier Lucas, DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). Lucas moved from questionable to out on Friday night. After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight, but his status changed from questionable to out Friday night. home.blurb: Junior Xavier Lucas , who hasn't played since the season opener against Stanford , is listed as questionable for Saturday, according to the Atlantic Coast Conference's first availability report for the game released on Wednesday. Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out. As for Clemson, two players are listed as questionable (defensive end Armon Mason and Elyjah Thurmon), while seven have been ruled out (safety Polo Anderson, cornerback Shavar Young Jr., wide receiver Cole Turner , running back David Eziomume, defensive tackles Kourtney Kelly and Markus Strong, and offensive lineman Mason Wade).
